title: $\gamma_d$ is surjective for $d\geq g$
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], of genus $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus]. For $d\in\mathbf Z$ let $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ be the subfunctor of the Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ [def-pc-picard-functor] on $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ of the classes whose fibrewise degree [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] is identically $d$. Let $d\geq g$, let $H_d$ be a $k$-scheme representing $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor], let $P_d$ be a $k$-scheme representing $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, and let $\gamma_d:H_d\to P_d$ be the morphism $D\mapsto\mathcal O(D)$ of [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]. Then $\gamma_d$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clause (5) 'the morphisms gamma_d are surjective for d >= g', and its proof, fourth paragraph: 'Let d >= g. Then for any field extension K/k and any invertible O_{X_K}-module L of degree d, chi(X_K, L) = d+1-g > 0. Hence L has a nonzero section and we conclude that L = O_{X_K}(D) for some divisor D of degree d. It follows that gamma_d is surjective'

proof.text: *The curve over a field extension.* Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and $C_K=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change]. The curve $C$ is integral, hence nonempty, and smooth over the separably closed field $k$, so it has a $k$-rational point $\sigma$ [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. Hence by [prop-pc-xk-integral] (2) $C_K$ is a smooth projective curve over $K$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] (in particular integral, of dimension $1$, and proper over $K$ [lem-pc-projective-proper]), with $H^0(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})=K$ and $\dim_KH^1(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=g$. By [lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim], applied to the smooth projective curve $C_K$ over $K$, $H^i(C_K,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\geq2$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$, and by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] $H^0,H^1$ of a coherent $\mathcal F$ are finite-dimensional over $K$; so for every coherent $\mathcal F$ on $C_K$ the Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic] is $\chi(C_K,\mathcal F)=\dim_KH^0(C_K,\mathcal F)-\dim_KH^1(C_K,\mathcal F)$. In particular $\chi(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})=1-g$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, fourth paragraph: 'for any field extension K/k ... chi(X_K, L) = d+1-g' (the value chi(X_K, O) = 1-g and the base change of X to K)

proof.text: *A $K$-point of $P_d$ is an invertible module of degree $d$ on $C_K$.* Let $y:\operatorname{Spec}K\to P_d$ be a morphism over $k$. Under the representing isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}\cong h_{P_d}$ [def-pc-representable-functor], $y$ corresponds to a class $\xi\in\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ [def-pc-picard-functor]. Since $C$ is a smooth projective curve with the $k$-rational point $\sigma$ (step 1), the hypotheses of [thm-pc-pic-split] hold for $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-pc-rational-hyp]; with $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $C_T=C_K$, the map $\operatorname{Pic}(C_K)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ is surjective, so $\xi$ is the class of an invertible $\mathcal O_{C_K}$-module $\mathcal L$. Computing the degree of $\xi$ with the trivial covering $\{\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}K\}$ and the representative $\mathcal L$ [def-pd-degree-morphism], its value at the unique point $t$ of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the fibrewise degree $\deg_T(\mathcal L)(t)$ [def-pd-fibrewise-degree]; as $\kappa(t)=K$, $C_{\kappa(t)}=C_K$ and $\mathcal L_t=\mathcal L$, this is $\deg_{C_K}(\mathcal L)=\chi(C_K,\mathcal L)-\chi(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. As $\xi\in\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$, $\deg_{C_K}(\mathcal L)=d$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, fourth paragraph: 'any invertible O_{X_K}-module L of degree d' (K-points of Pic^d as invertible modules of degree d; the proof's first paragraph: Pic_{X/k} is isomorphic to Pic_{X/k,sigma})

proof.text: *$\mathcal L$ has a nonzero section.* By steps 1 and 2, $\chi(C_K,\mathcal L)=\deg_{C_K}(\mathcal L)+\chi(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})=d+1-g\geq1$, since $d\geq g$. By step 1, $\chi(C_K,\mathcal L)=\dim_KH^0(C_K,\mathcal L)-\dim_KH^1(C_K,\mathcal L)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic], so $\dim_KH^0(C_K,\mathcal L)\geq\chi(C_K,\mathcal L)\geq1$. Choose $s\in H^0(C_K,\mathcal L)=\Gamma(C_K,\mathcal L)$ with $s\neq0$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, fourth paragraph: 'chi(X_K, L) = d+1-g > 0. Hence L has a nonzero section'

proof.text: *$\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)$ for $D=Z(s)$.* $C_K$ is integral (step 1) and $s\neq0$, so the zero scheme $D:=Z(s)\subseteq C_K$ [def-pc-zero-scheme] is an effective Cartier divisor, its ideal sheaf being an effective Cartier ideal [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier]. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] (with $X=C_K$, $\mathcal M=\mathcal O_{C_K}$, $\mathcal N=\mathcal L$, $\varphi=(f\mapsto fs)$, so that $Z(\varphi)=Z(s)=D$), $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)\otimes\mathcal O_{C_K}\cong\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)$, with $\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, fourth paragraph: 'we conclude that L = O_{X_K}(D) for some divisor D in X_K' (Divisors, Lemmas 02OR (4) and 01X0 (2))

proof.text: *$D$ is a $K$-point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$.* $C_K$ is proper over $K$ of dimension $1$ (step 1), and $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor on it (step 4); by [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-finite-over-field] $D$ is affine, $D\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite and $A:=\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra, so $D=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-pc-degree-base-change] (2), $\deg_{C_K}(\mathcal O_{C_K}(D))=\dim_KA$. Isomorphic coherent modules have isomorphic cohomology, hence the same $\chi$ and the same degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]; so by step 4 and step 2, $\dim_KA=\deg_{C_K}(\mathcal O_{C_K}(D))=\deg_{C_K}(\mathcal L)=d$. The morphism $D=\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]: it is finite; it is flat because $A$ is a free $K$-module (a vector space); it is locally of finite presentation because the finite-dimensional $K$-algebra $A$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $K$, hence finitely presented; and its only fibre is $D$ itself, with $\dim_K\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)=d$. As $D$ is a closed subscheme of $C_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=C_K$, $D\in\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ [def-pc-hilb-functor].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, fourth paragraph: 'for some divisor D in X_K of degree d' (D a point of Hilb^d_{X/k} with values in K)

proof.text: *The $K$-point $y$ lifts to $H_d$.* Since $H_d$ represents $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$ [def-pc-representable-functor], the element $D\in\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ of step 5 corresponds to a $k$-morphism $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to H_d$. By [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism] (3), the $K$-point $\gamma_d\circ x$ of $P_d$ corresponds to the class of $\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)$ in $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$. By step 4, $\mathcal O_{C_K}(D)\cong\mathcal L$, so this class is the image of $[\mathcal L]$, which is $\xi$ (step 2). The representing isomorphism being a bijection $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}K,P_d)$ under which $\xi$ corresponds to $y$, we get $\gamma_d\circ x=y$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, fourth paragraph: 'It follows that gamma_d is surjective' (the K-point lifts along gamma_d, by the construction of gamma_d in the proof's second paragraph)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Let $p\in P_d$ and $K:=\kappa(p)$ its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]; through the structure morphism $P_d\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $K$ is a field extension of $k$ [def-weil-residue-field], and the canonical morphism $j_p:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)\to P_d$ [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] ($\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\mathcal O_{P_d,p}\to\kappa(p)$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{P_d,p}\to P_d$) is a morphism over $k$ mapping the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to $p$. Steps 1 to 6 with $y=j_p$ give $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to H_d$ with $\gamma_d\circ x=j_p$; if $q\in H_d$ is the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ under $x$, then $\gamma_d(q)=j_p(\mathrm{pt})=p$. Hence every point of $P_d$ is in the image of $\gamma_d$, i.e. $\gamma_d$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 0BA0, proof, fourth paragraph, read in pic.tex (tag verified in tags/tags). The single sentence is written out in seven steps: (1) C has a k-point (separably closed k), so C_K is a smooth projective curve with H^0=K, h^1=g, cohomology vanishing above 1, chi = h^0 - h^1 and chi(O)=1-g; (2) a K-point y of P_d is a class xi in Pic^d(Spec K), represented by an invertible L on C_K (Pic(C_K) -> Pic_{C/k}(Spec K) onto by 0B9N/0B9U) of degree d (degree of a class through the trivial covering); (3) chi(L)=d+1-g>=1 so h^0(L)>=1 (no Riemann-Roch theorem is needed: the degree is defined as chi(L)-chi(O)); (4) on the integral C_K, Z(s) of a nonzero s is an effective Cartier divisor D and L = O(D) (two new nodes, Stacks 02OR(4)/01WZ and 01X0(2)); (5) D is finite over K of length deg O(D) = d, so finite locally free of degree d, a K-point of Hilb^d; (6) its point x of H_d satisfies gamma_d o x = y by clause (3) of [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]; (7) with K = kappa(p) every point p of P_d is hit. Statement unchanged. No slopmaster2 declaration states the item (grep of the id, of 'Hilb' and of Picard/Jacobian.lean: the surjectivity is only described in the docstring of the sorry isProper_of_representableBy_picardFunctorDegree_genus). Tools of other units used as black boxes: lem-pc-cartier-divisor-finite-over-field and lem-pc-degree-base-change (sk-thm-picard-rr), prop-pc-xk-integral and lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim (sk-thm-picard-twist), lem-pc-rational-hyp/thm-pc-pic-split (sk-prop-picard-pic-split), lem-pc-rational-points-dense (sk-prop-picard-dense-points), lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined (sk-thm-picard-rr); all are units the unit sk-prop-jacobian cites, directly or through them.
